analyst.summary: Adani Power had a strong-looking FY26 on the surface - profit up modestly for the year and up 64% in the final quarter - but a large part of that came from one-time regulatory income recognition and a lower tax bill, not from the underlying power business, which actually shrank slightly (revenue and operating profit both down about 1-2% year-on-year) as India's electricity-demand growth slowed sharply and spot power prices fell. The company is now borrowing heavily (debt up 40% in a year) to fund a large, multi-year plant-expansion plan that is still early in construction, and it continues to face periodic payment delays from its Bangladesh power customer. With the stock near a 52-week high and trading at a rich 32-37 times earnings - pricing in a much stronger growth path than the latest results actually show - we would use strength to reduce exposure rather than add or hold through the current valuation.
